messages:
Ava Park: Morning — quick async huddle. What I did: landed PR #4123 to add route-priority and header-based routing for /v1/edges. Blockers: auth-middleware unit test failing in CI (flaky token setup). Today: triage test + bump canary to 20% if green.
Ben Li: Noted. I saw ~3xx->503 spikes overnight tied to old rate policy on /v1/edges. I pushed a debug log to staging: `gw:rate_policy=legacy` — see logs: https://logs.redwood/staging/edge/523
Priya Rao: Thanks Ben — re: PR #4123, left a small CR comment around prioritized match order. Can we make it deterministic? Also add a unit that covers header-absent case.
Marco Gutierrez: I can take the flaky auth test. Repro locally with `make test-auth` — failing on token refresh mock. Will submit a fix by EOD.
Ava Park: @Marco thanks. If you need the mock helper I added in `pkg/auth/testutils.go` (linked in PR).
deploy-bot: canary rollout started for `api-gateway@4123` -> cluster-a (10%): deploy_id=depl-20260315-78
Ivy Chen: small ask — any config change needed for Dedicated customers? Rate-limit policy defaults might be stricter. If so, tag the config change and I'll coordinate docs + console flag.
Ben Li: Good call Ivy. PR includes a `default_rate_policy: standard` flag. If customers override, we honor `customer_policy` at route level.
Priya Rao: On determinism: instead of iteration order, sort matches by (priority desc, created_at asc). Added a code snippet in CR.
Ava Park: Sounds good. I'll update tests to assert ordering.
Marco Gutierrez: Pushed fix for auth test -> PR #4130. CI green locally, running full pipeline now.
deploy-bot: canary at 20% (cluster-a) -> no errors reported in past 12m. Observability: latency p50 stable, token failure rate dropped.
Ava Park: OK pushing to 50% once CI passes. Quick asks: @Priya can you add a small note in the config schema about `default_rate_policy`? @Ivy will you flag enterprise docs? :thumbsup:
Priya Rao: On it — will add schema note and an example snippet.
Ivy Chen: Yep, will flag docs + create advisory email for Dedicated customers if we flip defaults.
Ben Li: FYI I'll keep monitoring staging; ping me if you want me to roll back the canary.
Ava Park: Thanks everyone. If nothing else, I'll call this done for today.
